PR #1888 RE-REVIEW (findings 6/7/8 + .gitignore/AC14). Evidence from full-file reads of bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart, bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart (all 1980 lines), bin/fah_dap_command.dart, bin/fah.dart + part files (fah_runapp/fah_util/fah_model/fah_io/fah_wire_host/fah_trajectory), lib/src/plugins/plugin.dart, docs/dap.md §15, .gitignore, test/hub/dap_scoped_memberships_test.dart, test/hub/hub_plugin_host_test.dart. NOTE: this environment has NO shell/exec tool — `dart test` could NOT be run; test claims verified by reading only.

SUMMARY: F6 PARTIAL (mechanics fixed, but cleanupOverlay has ZERO production call sites). F7 VERIFIED. F8 PARTIAL (per-entry decode + test fixed, but loadWarnings is never surfaced by any host). .gitignore/AC14 VERIFIED.

=== FINDING 6 — runtime overlay — PARTIAL ===
(a) stable name + 0600 + atomic write: VERIFIED.
- Stable per-$HOME name: bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart `_initScopedMemberships`: `final runtimeDir = '$home/.dap/runtime'; final overlay = '$runtimeDir/channels.json';` — no pid. Field doc on `overlayChannelsFile` (bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart ~:86-96) documents the stable-name rationale.
- Atomic write: `_writeJsonAtomic` (bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:857-873) writes `$file.tmp` (flush) then `rename`; `seedOverlay` (:475-487) passes `mode0600: true` → `chmod 600` (:866-871). Vendored client pointed at the overlay via `_environment[hub.envChannelsFile] = overlay`.
- Nits: chmod runs AFTER rename → transient umask-mode window on the target; a crash between tmp-write and rename leaves `channels.json.tmp` which `sweepLegacyOverlays` never cleans (it only matches `channels-<pid>.json`, :531-537).

(b) cleanupOverlay actually called on shutdown: NOT FIXED — ZERO call sites.
- `cleanupOverlay` exists at bin/fah_dap_scoped.dart:497-504 (matches claimed :493-500) with an honest doc comment: "Hosts with a teardown path (plugin dispose / CLI finally) call this…".
- But no host has a teardown path: the `FahPlugin` interface (lib/src/plugins/plugin.dart) has ONLY `name` + `register` — no dispose. `HubPluginHost` (bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart, read in full) defines no dispose and never references cleanupOverlay.
- Every shutdown path in bin/fah_runapp.dart was read: headless `try { code = await _headlessRun } finally { sigintSub.cancel(); drainStdoutLines(); logTeeFile?.closeSync(); } exit(code)`; REPL `try { await cli.run(); } finally { sigintSub.cancel(); logTeeFile?.closeSync(); }`; `exitInteractive130` (finally: exit(130)); `_gracefulHeadlessExit` (fah_util.dart). NONE call cleanupOverlay. bin/fah_dap_command.dart (`fa dap` verbs) never boots the scoped service. fah_trajectory/import/serve branches exit before plugin boot.
- CONSEQUENCE: the plaintext-key overlay `~/.dap/runtime/channels.json` persists after every normal exit (SIGKILL excepted). Growth/unbounded-accumulation IS fixed (one stable file + boot sweep of legacy per-pid names), but "plaintext keys never outlive the run" is NOT achieved — only the next boot's seedOverlay rewrites the file. The rework claim "cleanupOverlay … deletes on shutdown" is inaccurate; docs/dap.md hedges it ("deleted on clean shutdown WHERE THE HOST HAS A TEARDOWN PATH", ~:735), and this host has none.

(c) prune/keep-on-doubt: VERIFIED with caveats. Claimed `_pruneStaleOverlay` does not exist by that name — the actual function is `sweepLegacyOverlays` (:512-527), called once at plugin registration (fah_hub_plugin.dart `_initScopedMemberships`). Keep-on-doubt guard: `_pidAlive` (:539-548) — Linux `/proc/<pid>`, else `kill -0`, and `on Object → return true` (:546, "unknown — keep the file rather than delete live keys"). Liveness = pid alive, NOT mtime/age. Shared/multi-user HOME risk: low on Linux (/proc answers for other users' processes). On macOS, `kill -0` on ANOTHER USER'S process returns EPERM (exitCode≠0) → treated dead → could delete a live concurrent agent's LEGACY overlay in a shared HOME (narrow; the stable channels.json is never touched by the sweep). Concurrent agents sharing one HOME also clobber each other's stable overlay on every re-seed (accepted by design, but note cleanupOverlay — if ever wired — would need the same keep-on-doubt guard it lacks).

(d) docs: VERIFIED. docs/dap.md §15.3 (~:725-740) names `~/.dap/runtime/channels.json`, 0600, "ONE stable name per $HOME, rewritten atomically on every re-seed, never per-pid", the boot sweep, and the honest "deleted on clean shutdown where the host has a teardown path" hedge.

(e) test: EXISTS — test/hub/dap_scoped_memberships_test.dart end of file (~:446-486): 'cleanupOverlay deletes the overlay file (best-effort)' and 'sweepLegacyOverlays removes pid files of dead processes only' (dead pid file deleted, live-pid file kept, stable channels.json never touched; missing-dir tolerated). NOT RUN (no exec tool). Test covers the unit only — nothing wires cleanupOverlay into a host, so no integration coverage of the gap in (b).
